section: Panchayati Raj and urban bodies in Andhra Pradesh - structure, elections, finances, performance
subsections: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode
AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 - three tiers

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 primarily governs which of the following?
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 governs Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats.
accepted.tq: Match the statute with the exact category of local bodies governed by it.
accepted.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 33.33 per cent reservation for Backward Classes in Andhra Pradesh urban local bodies:
1. It is implemented under the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act, 1994.
2. It is also implemented under the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965.
3. It is provided exclusively under the Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 33.33 per cent BC quota is implemented under the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 and the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965. It is not stated to be exclusively under the Panchayat Raj Act.
accepted.tq: Identify the correctly associated laws and reject the exclusive claim in statement 3.
accepted.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who introduced the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024?
o: The Chairperson of the Zilla Parishad
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Municipal Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024 was introduced by Municipal Minister P. Narayana.
accepted.tq: Use the person–legislation association; APPSC commonly tests the minister responsible for introducing a Bill.
accepted.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024:
1. It was passed without debate in the Assembly.
2. It reversed an earlier amendment.
3. It restored the two-child restriction for municipal election candidates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Bill was passed without debate and reversed an earlier amendment. It removed, rather than restored, the two-child restriction.
accepted.tq: Find the false statement by checking the direction of the legal change.
accepted.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal purpose of the 2024 amendment relating to municipal elections in Andhra Pradesh was to:
o: Transfer municipal elections to the Union Election Commission
Remove the two-child norm for contesting municipal elections
Introduce direct election of all councillors
Create a new intermediate rural tier
accepted.x: The amendment removed the restriction that barred persons with more than two children from contesting municipal elections.
accepted.tq: Apply the stated legal purpose to identify the precise consequence of the amendment.
accepted.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the companion legislative change relating to rural local bodies in Andhra Pradesh?
o: A companion Bill removed the two-child bar for panchayat elections in November 2024.
The Panchayat Raj Act was repealed in November 2024.
A companion Bill introduced a two-child bar for panchayat elections in November 2024.
The Bill transferred panchayat elections to municipalities.
accepted.x: A companion Bill removed the two-child bar on contesting panchayat elections in November 2024.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between removal and introduction of a qualification restriction.
accepted.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Municipal Laws (Third Amendment) Bill, 2026 provides for:
o: A Uniform Mutation Fee on title transfers in municipal records
Direct election of Mandal Parishad Presidents
A new tax on Gram Sabha meetings
A uniform age of 25 years for municipal candidates
accepted.x: The Third Amendment Bill, 2026 adds a Uniform Mutation Fee on title transfers recorded in municipal records.
accepted.tq: Link the amendment Bill with its specific administrative and financial provision.
accepted.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to the mode of election of Mayors in Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following is correct?
o: Mayors have so far been elected directly by all residents of the corporation.
Mayors have so far been elected by Gram Sabhas.
Mayors have so far been elected indirectly from among the councillors.
Mayors have so far been nominated by the Governor.
accepted.x: Until the proposed change, Mayors in Andhra Pradesh were elected indirectly from among the councillors or corporators.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the existing indirect mode from the later proposal for direct election.
accepted.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

accepted.s: On 18 August 2026, the Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approved direct election of which office-holders?
o: Mandal Parishad Presidents and Zilla Parishad Chairpersons
All members of District Planning Committees
Mayors of Corporations and Chairpersons of Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats
accepted.x: The Cabinet approved direct election of Mayors of Corporations and Chairpersons of Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats.
accepted.tq: Use the scope of the decision to separate urban offices from rural Panchayati Raj offices.
accepted.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding Andhra Pradesh municipal legislation mentioned in 2026?
accepted.x: The laws named in the 2026 context are the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 and the Municipal Corporations Act, 1955.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure statute–year pair and reject the swapped years.
accepted.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 is identified as which Act?
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 is Act No. 13 of 1994.
accepted.tq: Test the exact Act number, a common numerical trap in legislation questions.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 - three tiers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 was enacted primarily to:
o: Confer constitutional status on Municipal Corporations
Give effect to the 73rd Constitutional Amendment
accepted.x: The Act was enacted to give effect to the 73rd Constitutional Amendment relating to Panchayati Raj institutions.
accepted.tq: Identify the purpose of the statute rather than its administrative details.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 - three tiers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the size of the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994?
accepted.x: The Act contains 278 sections arranged in 8 Parts.
accepted.tq: Treat the section count and Part count as a paired numerical fact.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 - three tiers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Part)
 a. Part II
 b. Part III
 c. Part IV
 d. Part VI

List-II (Subject)
 i. Finance Commission
 ii. Gram Panchayat
 iii. Mandal Parishads
 iv. Zilla Parishads
accepted.x: Part II deals with Gram Panchayats, Part III with Mandal Parishads, Part IV with Zilla Parishads and Part VI with the Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Start from the known Part II–Gram Panchayat pair and complete the statutory mapping.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 - three tiers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly gives the subjects covered by Parts V and VI of the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994?
o: Gram Panchayat and Mandal Parishads, respectively
accepted.x: Part V deals with elections, while Part VI deals with the Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between adjacent statutory Parts by their subject headings.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 - three tiers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The distinctive intermediate tier in Andhra Pradesh's Panchayati Raj system is the:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh uses the Mandal Parishad as its intermediate tier, unlike the Panchayat Samiti terminology used in most States.
accepted.tq: Test the State-specific terminology against the familiar national term.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 - three tiers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gram Panchayat under the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994:
1. Its ward members are directly elected.
2. Its Sarpanch is directly elected.
3. Its term is five years.
4. The minimum age for contesting is 21 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Ward members and the Sarpanch are directly elected; the Gram Panchayat has a five-year term and the minimum contesting age is 21 years.
accepted.tq: Check each tier-specific feature separately before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 - three tiers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Mandal Parishad in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The President is elected indirectly from among ZPTC members.
MPTC members are directly elected and the President is elected indirectly from among them.
MPTC members are indirectly elected and the President is directly elected by all voters.
Both MPTC members and the President are nominated by the Governor.
accepted.x: MPTC members are directly elected, while the Mandal Parishad President is elected indirectly from among the MPTCs.
accepted.tq: Separate the election mode of members from that of the head.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 - three tiers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The head of a Zilla Parishad in Andhra Pradesh is elected:
o: By the Sarpanches of all Gram Panchayats
Indirectly from among the ZPTC members
Directly by all voters in the district
accepted.x: ZPTC members are directly elected, but the Zilla Parishad Chairperson is elected indirectly from among the ZPTC members.
accepted.tq: Use the member-versus-head distinction to identify the correct election mode.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 - three tiers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, which statement regarding chairpersons at the intermediate and district levels is correct?
o: They must be elected directly by the entire electorate.
They are elected indirectly, while the State determines the mode at the village level.
They are appointed by the State Election Commission.
They are selected by the Union Government.
accepted.x: The 73rd Amendment provides for indirect election of chairpersons at the intermediate and district levels, while the State determines the mode of election at the village level.
accepted.tq: Apply the constitutional distinction between higher-tier and village-level chairperson elections.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 - three tiers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What is the minimum age for contesting elections to any of the three Panchayati Raj tiers under the Andhra Pradesh framework described?
accepted.x: The minimum age for contesting Panchayati Raj elections is 21 years, consistent with the floor under Article 243F.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the minimum contesting age from the voting age and older qualification thresholds.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 - three tiers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mandal Parishad — President elected indirectly from MPTCs
Zilla Parishad — Chairperson elected directly by all district voters
accepted.x: The Zilla Parishad Chairperson is elected indirectly from among the ZPTC members, not directly by all district voters. The other pairs are correct.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed election mode in the otherwise correctly matched tier relationships.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 - three tiers  [APPSC]
